resources.string: Clearing only tombstones this phone\'s history and does not delete Windows history remotely.
No clips yet. Share text, use the Quick Settings tile, or pair with Windows.
That text is larger than 1 MiB and was not stored.
Not paired with Windows. Pairing is required before clips can sync.
Windows is unreachable. Clips stay on this phone until the peer is online.
Could not write to the system clipboard. Try again from the app.
Stop capturing and sending clips. Existing history is kept.
New clips are not stored or sent. Past clips are not backfilled later.
Write inbound Windows text to the system clipboard when public write works.
Keep a connected-device foreground service so the Windows link stays up. This is not clipboard permission.
After the phone restarts, try to restore the sync service. Off by default.
Skip captures from well-known password managers and authenticator apps. Does not apply to clips received from Windows.
Comma-separated Android package names. Entries with spaces are ignored.
Older clips are deleted on this device only. Windows keeps its own retention setting.
The export file contains clipboard bodies in plaintext.
Import restores local history only. Imported clips are not synced to Windows.
Text is larger than 1 MiB and was not sent.
Capture is paused or private mode is on.
That source app is blocked from capture.
Clipboard sent to Clip It Forward
Clipboard is empty or not text.
Copy inbound clips when they are not applied automatically.
Tap Copy to put it on this phone\'s clipboard.
Ongoing status for the Windows connection. Never includes clipboard text.
Keeping the Windows connection alive. This is not clipboard permission.
Background sync stopped after a restart. Open the app to resume.
Display-over-other-apps permission is required to read the clipboard from an overlay. This does not start a background service.
This device would need a touchable overlay to read the clipboard. Clip It Forward will not enable that.

This permission cannot be granted in-app. Use android-bootstrap.ps1 to print the exact adb grant and revoke commands for the selected device. The script never grants it for you. Install, upgrade, or reboot invalidates the grant; re-check after those events.
READ_LOGS is not granted. Copy the printed adb command and run it yourself.
Each permission is a separate card. Grant, skip, or re-check independently. Share, the Quick Settings tile, and foreground capture stay available.
Manual fallback is always available: share panel, Quick Settings tile, and foreground capture.
Show inbound copy actions and the ongoing sync notification.
Keep the Windows connection alive as a connected-device service. This is not clipboard permission.
Reduce OEM kills so background sync can resume after idle.
Briefly focus a 1x1 untouchable window so overlay polling or ADB-log reads can copy text.
Watch system clipboard-change logs as an event signal. The body is still read through overlay.
Start Clip It Forward\'s bundled privileged host so the clipboard UserService can run as shell. Official Shizuku already running is also accepted.
Confirm this app may use the privileged host. Preferred event-driven read mode.
A persistent sync notification is visible while the service runs.
A long-running service uses a little battery and stays in the notification shade.
The system may keep Clip It Forward awake more often.
A transparent window briefly takes focus during a read. It stays untouchable.
Log access is a privileged adb grant. Clip It Forward never stores or uploads raw log lines.
The host must be started as shell after each reboot. The printed adb command is never run for you.
The host runs with shell privileges limited to clipboard binder calls.
Notification actions and inbound copy prompts stay hidden. The service can still run.
Background connection will not stay up. Use the app in the foreground.
The OEM may kill the process. You will need to reopen the app.
Overlay polling and ADB-log read modes stay unavailable. Overlay is never enabled without consent.
ADB log event mode stays unavailable. Re-check after install, upgrade, or reboot if you grant it later.
Privileged event mode stays unavailable until you authorize the app.
READ_LOGS is granted only via adb (android-bootstrap.ps1). There is never an in-app dialog. Re-check after install, upgrade, or reboot.

The bundled host is started only via adb/root already running as shell (android-bootstrap.ps1). Clip It Forward never runs that command. After each reboot, start it again. Official Shizuku already running is also accepted.
If the preferred mode fails, try the next allowed mode. Overlay still requires explicit consent.
Off by default. Overlay is not used for write. Public clipboard write stays the default.
Some ROMs (e.g. MIUI) deny background clipboard reads system-side, so overlay polling may only capture while Clip It Forward is in the foreground. Run the self-test to verify on this device.
Upload captured clipboard text while the app is in the background.
Write inbound Windows text with the public clipboard API. No overlay required.
Write defaults to the public clipboard API. Overlay is not required for write.
Writes app-generated random text, verifies it, then clears it. Your own clipboard content is never read, kept, or uploaded.
Notifications are hidden. The sync service can still run; clipboard access is separate.
Scanning a new code replaces the current pairing after your confirmation.
Open Clip It Forward on your computer, choose \"Pair new device\", then scan the QR code it shows.
Camera permission was denied. You can still pair by pasting the payload below.
Only continue if the name and certificate fingerprint below match what the Windows app shows.
Warning: this computer\'s certificate CHANGED since the last pairing. If you did not reinstall Clip It Forward on Windows, stop and check the computer.
Approve this phone in the Clip It Forward window on \"%1$s\".
This phone is now paired with \"%1$s\". Clipboard sync starts in a later stage; the trust and secret are stored securely now.
That is not a valid Clip It Forward pairing code.
This code identifies this device itself.
The computer presented a DIFFERENT certificate than the QR code promised. Pairing was blocked. Check the network and re-open the QR window on Windows.
The computer could not be reached. Make sure both devices are on the same network.
The request was rejected on the computer.
The computer did not approve in time. Show a fresh QR code and try again.
This code was already used or cancelled. Show a fresh QR code.
This code expired. Show a fresh QR code and scan it promptly.
Too many pairing attempts. Wait a minute, then show a fresh QR code and try again.
The computer answered outside the pairing protocol. Update both apps to matching versions.
